summary: The audit counts your graduate units toward the 90 the degree needs, leaving out courses numbered below 100 and any AA 300 thesis units past 24. You check by hand the 21 units of approved advanced courses beyond the M.S. (move them in), the advisor-approved course proposal at candidacy, the 3.0 GPA and the thesis.

totals.label: Courses below the 100 level
totals.why: "All units must be in courses at or above the 100 level."

totals.label: Engineer thesis (AA 300)
totals.why: "Students may register for up to 24 units of Engineer thesis."

taz8r0tl.why: "Engineer’s Degree candidates must complete a minimum of 90 units" (the Bulletin's program minimum, which the audit checks). "a student must complete a minimum of 21 units of approved courses in advanced study in engineering, science, and mathematics (excluding research, directed study, and seminars) beyond the M.S. degree. These units must be taken for a letter grade, and all courses must be numbered 200 and above." "An advisor approved Engineer’s Degree course proposal must be submitted when applying for Engineer’s Degree candidacy." "A minimum cumulative grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 is required". The approved courses have no list, so they are moved in by hand.

children.name: 21 units of approved advanced courses (200+, letter grade, no research or seminars) beyond the M.S.
Advisor-approved course proposal submitted with the candidacy application
Cumulative GPA of 3.0, including the courses on the candidacy form
